Hi Soojin,

Quick intro — I'm on ClearSky's procurement team (contracts@clearsky.ai). We're evaluating Redwood for a production rollout (approx 8M tokens/month steady-state) and need clarity on how you package SLA / premium support. A few specific asks to help us compare options:

- A compact matrix showing uptime tiers (99.5 / 99.9 / 99.95), typical monthly crediting formula, and associated per-month retainer pricing for an "oncall retainer" (i.e., dedicated triage/engineer for escalations).
- Whether retainer fees offset credits (and if so, how — e.g., retainer reduces credit liability by $X).
- Sample MSA language for SLA credits and oncall scope (we'll need redlines for procurement/legal).
- Any onboarding or pilot discounts you offer for the first 3–6 months.

Can you send a short set of options we can present to our team by EOD Monday (PST)? If easier, a 30-min call early next week to walk through options would work too — Julia (cc'd) will coordinate.

Thanks,
Contracts Team
ClearSky Analytics

Hi — thanks for the clear list, happy to put together a compact matrix. I've attached our internal SLA_pricing_playbook.xlsx and a mutual_action_plan.docx that map packaging menus to recommended usage bands.

High level — two ways customers typically buy this:
1) Commit + credits: a usage/commit tier that sets your base uplift and credit slabs for uptime shortfalls. Lower upfront, predictable credits when you miss targets.
2) Hybrid (what we often recommend for mid-stage deployments): a base commit + small monthly oncall retainer that buys faster escalation windows and reduces the severity-based credit exposure.

I'll loop Rishi and Marissa for pricing ranges and a recommended call script. Julia — can you share the name of your billing/contact for PO and preferred time windows for a 30-min sync?

Best,

Subject: Internal: ClearSky pricing options (draft ranges)

Soojin / Marissa — quick draft numbers to feed back to ClearSky. Assumptions: 8M tokens/month steady-state, US region, 3-year ROI target for larger commit. Values are monthly list (USD).

Option A — Conservative (Commit + Credits)
- 99.5% uptime band: base fee $8,000 / month, credit formula: 10% of monthly fee per 0.1% below target up to 50% cap
- 99.9% uptime band: base fee $18,000 / month, credit formula: 7% per 0.05% below target, cap 40%

Option B — Hybrid (recommended for ClearSky)
- Base fee: $12,000 / month (near 99.9 baseline)
- Oncall retainer: $6,500 / month (dedicated escalation SLA: <60m triage, dedicated engineer during business hours; <4h triage outside BH)
- Credit exposure: reduced by 50% if retainer active (i.e., retainer offsets credit liability dollar-for-dollar up to retainer amount when invoiceable incidents occur)

Option C — Premium (Full coverage)
- Base fee: $25,000 / month, oncall retainer included, 99.95 target, credits limited to 20% cap, faster RTO guarantees for critical incidents.

Notes / tradeoffs:
- For hybrid we recommend a 6-month introductory 15% discount on the oncall retainer (not on base fee) to accelerate adoption.
- If procurement insists on credit-offset language in MSA, we should limit the offset to incident-class credits (exclude systemic degradations that require product fixes) — legal will want this clarified.

I'll prepare a short one-pager with the three options and expected TCV over 12/24 months.

— Rishi
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>, Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 31 Aug 2026 09:14:00 -07:00
Subject: RE: Internal: ClearSky pricing options (draft ranges)

All — good start. A few adjustments I recommend before sending externally:

- Offer: 15% reduction on the oncall retainer for first 6 months (Rishi suggested that) and include a one-time professional services credit of $7,500 for runbook/onboarding.
- Clarify the offset: make it explicit in the MSA that the retainer offsets customer credits only for incidents where Redwood met the triage SLA but failed long-term availability due to transient infrastructure — excludes product regressions or customer integration issues. This protects us from having the retainer be a blanket waiver.
- Add a short pilot option: 3-month pilot at a reduced base fee of $6,000/month + $3,250 retainer (15% discount applied) with a capped credit exposure to accelerate decisioning. We can convert pilot credits to TCV if they adopt.

I'll run the MSA redline with legal and upload a first pass (MSA_redline_v1.docx). Once legal confirms the offset language, we can share externally plus a brief decision matrix.

-Marissa

Subject: Proposed SLA packaging — 3 options and next steps

Hi Julia / Contracts Team — thanks for the ask and for the patience while we pulled internal numbers together. Attached is a concise 1-pager + the MSA redline (MSA_redline_v1.docx) and the pricing playbook. Below are three options we recommend for ClearSky based on your stated volume.

Option 1 — Pilot (low friction)
- 3-month pilot: $6,000 / month base + $3,250 / month oncall retainer (15% introductory discount applied)
- Credit exposure capped at 25% of monthly fee for the pilot term
- One-time onboarding PS credit: $7,500 applied to first invoice

Option 2 — Hybrid (recommended)
- Base fee: $12,000 / month + $6,500 / month oncall retainer
- Retainer offsets credits up to the retainer amount for incident classes covered by the triage SLA (see redline for exact language)
- 6-month 15% discount on retainer during ramp period

Option 3 — Premium (SLA-first)
- Base fee: $25,000 / month, included oncall retainer, 99.95% uptime target, credit cap 20%

Next steps:
1) Please review the attached MSA_redline_v1 and confirm if procurement/legal want a call with our Legal lead to walk through the offset language.
2) If you prefer, we can book a 30-min alignment call this week to pick a preferred option and agree a timeline. Suggested times: Wed 09/02 10:00 or Thu 09/03 14:00 PT.
3) Please share the billing contact for PO issuance and the internal technical contact who will own onboarding.

Recommended by Redwood: Option 2 (Hybrid) — it balances predictability and escalations for an 8M token/month workload while limiting initial TCV.

Best regards,
Soojin Lee
